drhp.business: Mercury EV-Tech Limited manufactures electric two-wheelers, three-wheelers, passenger vehicles, buses and loaders, together with in-house manufacture of key components such as batteries, chassis and motor controllers, supported by a captive Cathodic Electrodeposition (CED) coating facility. The Company has expanded through subsidiaries engaged in tractors, automotive components, lithium-ion battery manufacturing and passenger EVs, positioning it across multiple segments of the EV value chain rather than as a single-product vehicle manufacturer.
drhp.end_markets: Institutional/fleet buyers|Retail buyers|Rural and Tier-II/III cities
drhp.expansion: The Company continued to strengthen its vertical integration and expand its presence through subsidiaries engaged in tractors, automotive components, lithium-ion battery manufacturing and passenger EVs, positioning it across multiple segments of the EV value chain. During the year, the Company continued to strengthen its manpower base to support capacity expansion, new product development, and the scale-up of its battery and component manufacturing operations. Risk mitigation for technology obsolescence references 'phased capacity expansion' as an ongoing measure.

risks.note: Rated High. Prices of lithium, cobalt, nickel, copper and other battery raw materials are subject to global commodity cycles and currency fluctuations, which could impact cost of production and margins.
Rated High. The EV space has attracted established automobile majors as well as numerous new entrants, resulting in pricing pressure and margin compression across vehicle categories.
Rated Medium. Any reduction, withdrawal, delay or restructuring of Central/State subsidy schemes could adversely affect near-term demand and the pricing competitiveness of EVs versus ICE vehicles.

Rated Medium. Rapid changes in battery chemistry, charging standards and vehicle technology could render existing product lines or capacities less competitive if the Company is unable to keep pace with innovation.

Rated Medium. Successful integration of recently acquired subsidiaries and new manufacturing facilities carries execution risk in terms of operational alignment, capital allocation and realisation of anticipated synergies.
Rated Medium. Relates to prudent capital structure and monitoring of debt-equity levels amid diversified funding sources for capacity expansion.
Limited availability of affordable vehicle financing for EV buyers and uneven charging infrastructure across geographies could restrain the pace of adoption.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Industry-wide retail EV sales have grown steadily, with overall EV penetration of new vehicle sales rising from around 5.3% in FY 2022-23 to an estimated 8.5% in FY 2025-26.
- Growing fuel costs, tightening emission norms, State and Central Government incentives, and rising consumer and fleet-operator awareness of total cost of ownership are driving sustained EV demand.
- Government programmes such as the PLI scheme for Automobile and Auto Components, the PM E-DRIVE scheme, and State-level EV policies are encouraging domestic manufacturing and localisation of the EV supply chain.
